lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Where are the beautiful men and women, Hermes? I'm new here. Give me the tour.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: I don't have time, Menippus. But look over there—to the right. That's where Hyacinthus is, and Narcissus, and Nireus, and Achilles, and Tyro, and Helen, and Leda. The whole vintage-beauty section, basically.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: I see bones. Mostly skulls with the meat off. They look much the same.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Yes, well, those are the bones all the poets keep going on about. The ones you seem to be taking rather lightly.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Still, show me Helen. I couldn't pick her out myself.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And for this they filled a thousand ships from all Greece? For this all those Greeks and barbarians died, and all those cities were razed?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: You never saw the woman alive, Menippus. If you had, you would have said yourself there was nothing outrageous about 'suffering long pains for such a woman.' Look at flowers: once they're dry and the colour has gone, of course they look shapeless. But when they're blooming, when they have their colour, they're magnificent.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: That's exactly what amazes me, Hermes: that the Achaeans didn't understand they were labouring over something so short-lived, and so very quick to lose its bloom.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: I don't have time to philosophise with you, Menippus. Pick a spot wherever you like, lie yourself down there, and I'll go collect the rest of the dead.
